primary_sources.title: Online control of the familywise error rate
verified_claims: Alpha-Spending uses an infinite nonnegative gamma sequence summing to one and tests H_i at alpha*gamma_i.
Online Fallback recycles rejection budget and Proposition 2 states strong FWER control for arbitrarily dependent p-values.
Online Fallback-1 has alpha_i = alpha*gamma_i + R_{i-1}*alpha_{i-1}.

primary_sources.title: Family-wise Error Rate Control with E-values
verified_claims: The e-Fallback construction is defined for a fixed sequence H_1->...->H_n with fixed initial alpha budgets summing to alpha.
Its sequential/always-valid discussion concerns e-processes evolving over data time for a fixed n-hypothesis family, with common filtration/stopping-time conditions.

findings.claim: Fresh conditionally valid audits with predictable alpha_j and pathwise sum_j alpha_j <= alpha_global control run-level probability of any false commit under arbitrary adaptive candidate generation/triage.
findings.derivation: Let F_{j-1} contain all development history and prior audit outcomes before fresh audit j; require the frozen candidate/hypothesis identity and its null status to be determined before current fresh outcomes, alpha_j to be F_{j-1}-measurable, and P(R_j=1 | F_{j-1}, H_j true) <= alpha_j. Then P(any false commit) <= E[sum_j 1{H_j true} R_j] <= E[sum_j 1{H_j true} alpha_j] <= E[sum_j alpha_j] <= alpha_global.
findings.scope: The result fails if alpha_j is chosen after current-audit outcomes, if the candidate is mutated using current confirmation outcomes before decision, if null-validity is only marginal when selection can destroy it, or if lifetime alpha can reset without an outer allocation.

findings.claim: Tian-Ramdas Online Fallback provides strong FWER under arbitrary p-value dependence and Fallback-1 uses the stated one-step recycling formula.
findings.evidence: Section 2.2 defines the general transfer-weight procedure and Proposition 2 states FWER control for arbitrarily dependent p-values; the special w_{k,i}=1{k=i-1} case gives alpha_i=alpha*gamma_i+R_{i-1}alpha_{i-1}.
findings.scope: The paper's theorem is written for an indexed online sequence of hypotheses/p-values.

findings.claim: The same fallback logic can be used for adaptively generated fresh-confirmation candidates when each candidate is frozen before audit and its null p-value is conditionally superuniform given prior history.
findings.derivation: Before the first false rejection, every recycled alpha mass can only flow through rejected nonnull hypotheses. Each base alpha mass is conserved/split forward by transfer weights whose outgoing sum is at most one; mass assigned to a true null is absorbed if that null is not rejected, and a rejection would be the first false event. With conditional superuniformity at predictable levels, summing first-false hazards over the conserved base mass gives at most alpha_global.
findings.scope: Treat this as a derived interface requiring pre-audit-measurable candidate/null identity and conditional validity, not as a verbatim Tian-Ramdas theorem about arbitrary data-dependent hypothesis creation.

findings.claim: Hartog-Lei e-Fallback can be dropped directly into an open-ended adaptively generated candidate stream without an additional family/interface argument.
findings.evidence: The paper defines e-Fallback on a fixed H_1->...->H_n family. Its sequential guarantees use e-processes indexed by data time for all i in [n] and common stopping/filtration conditions; this is different from an unbounded stream in which hypothesis identities themselves are created over time.
findings.scope: The paper still provides useful fixed-family e-value closure and always-valid machinery. It does not by itself close the worker's open-ended adaptive candidate-identity interface.

material_interpretation: The worker's alpha-spending firewall is technically sound under its stated conditional-freshness and lifetime-spend contract, and Online Fallback is a valid stronger recycling primitive under arbitrary dependence. The main remaining scope boundary is e-Fallback/closed-testing: Hartog-Lei's current theorem family is fixed-n, so an open-ended adaptive self-improvement stream still needs an explicit online conditional-e-value construction or a fixed-family/epoch embedding.

downstream_use.correction: Keep alpha-spending and Online Fallback as valid run-level multiplicity mechanisms only after candidate-level conditional freshness is established. Do not cite Hartog-Lei e-Fallback as direct proof for adaptively created unlimited candidate identities.
do_not_generalize: Arbitrary p-value dependence is not the same statement as arbitrary current-outcome-dependent candidate mutation.
A fixed-n e-Fallback family is not automatically an unbounded hypothesis-generation process.
Simulation FWER far below 0.05 in a short discrete e-process does not authorize increasing the theoretical alpha budget without separate calibration.
